subject: Renewal + Dedicated Pool Increase — SLA Exception for Throughput/Latency
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz@aureus.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase (Aureus)

Olga — thanks again for the QBR call last week. Aureus is ready to move forward with our annual renewal but we need to materially increase our Dedicated capacity for Q1: target is +16 GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent), with the option to burst another 8 for short windows.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm you can reserve a dedicated pool (24 GPUs total) starting Jan 15, 2027.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 24k tokens/sec (aggregate) during business hours; spike handling for up to 48k tokens/sec for 30m/day.
- Latency expectations: we'd like p95 < 120ms for interactive calls, but we understand this may require an SLA exception depending on pooling/placement.
- Contract: 12-month renewal with an expansion addendum. Procurement wants the price and SLA language to be explicit so we can approve quickly.

I attached our capacity forecast for the first two quarters. Please loop in pricing/CS/legal.

Thanks,
Liz Harper
Head of AI Platforms
Aureus Analytics

Liz — really appreciate the clear ask and the forecast. Happy to get this moving. High level response: we can reserve the additional GPUs and provision a 24-GPU dedicated pool for the Jan 15 cutover, with burst capacity available subject to capacity windows.

A few items we need to lock down from your side so we can finalize pricing and put together an SLA exception where needed:
- Confirm whether the 48k tokens/sec spike needs to be sustained from a single zone (we can provide multi-zone throughput but cross-zone adds complexity).
- Clarify whether the 120ms p95 target is a firm SLO or a best-effort target. If firm, we will need to submit an SLA exception for latency to Legal/RevOps.
- Preferred invoice/PO cadence and whether Aureus requires an annual prepay or monthly invoicing.

I'm looping in Ben (pricing/AM) and Marissa (CS) to propose a term sheet and cutover plan. We'll add Markus from Legal once we have a proposed redline for the SLA language.

Preliminary attachment: proposed_term_sheet_v3.docx (term sheet + price bands).

Next steps: Ben will send the commercial terms this week; Marissa will propose a cutover timeline; we'll produce an SLA-exception draft for your review.

Liz — adding some operational notes from CS so we can align on rollout risk and monitoring: 
- We recommend a phased provisioning: 12 GPUs reserved at cutover (Jan 15) + an add-on 12 GPUs after 30 days following traffic verification. That reduces migration risk and allows kernel-level tuning.
- We'll enable prefix/KV caching and an optimized batching profile for your largest routes; expected latency improvement ~10-15% once tuned.
- For the 48k tokens/sec spike windows: propose scheduled burst windows (two 30m windows/day) for the first 60 days; ad-hoc burst will be subject to availability.

Operational asks from Aureus for the cutover:
1) A 72-hour test window prior to go-live where you send synthetic traffic.
2) Production traffic ramp plan (10% -> 50% -> 90% over 3 days).
3) An on-call rotation for the first 14 days with an SRE contact.

We'll include these guardrails in the term sheet addendum and the cutover runbook. Happy to sync live this week if helpful.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

(Internal note: pricing flexibility may be required; Ben to advise.)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz@aureus.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase (Aureus) — SLA exception framework

Liz — thanks, and congrats on getting this prioritized internally. From Legal/Finance perspective we've reviewed the ask and can approve a limited SLA exception tied to the expanded dedicated pool under the following guardrails: 

1) Exception duration: 6 months from cutover date, after which standard SLA baseline applies unless mutually extended.
2) Latency SLO: we will accept p95 <= 150ms as the enforceable SLO for the first 6-month window (note: higher than your 120ms target). The term sheet will show both the target (120ms, non-binding) and the contractual SLO (150ms) with performance measurement defined by the Redwood Console metrics.
3) Throughput guarantee: Redwood will provide best-effort to sustain the 24k tokens/sec baseline; burst windows (defined in the addendum) will be scheduled and agreed in advance. We cannot commit to unscheduled sustained 48k tokens/sec without additional capacity reservations — we can support scheduled spikes up to 48k for up to 30 minutes/day during the 6-month exception.
4) Uptime credits: if monthly availability for the dedicated pool falls below 99.2% during the exception window, Aureus will be eligible for service credits pro-rated to the lost minutes (credit schedule attached). For outages caused by third-party infra (cloud provider) we will perform joint postmortems but credits will be capped per the addendum.
5) Signature & procurement: need countersignature on the SLA-exception-form.pdf and updated term sheet (attached). Procurement PO acceptable; if Aureus requires prepayment, finance will invoice accordingly.

I'll attach the formal exception form and the credit schedule for Aureus to review. Once countersigned we can schedule the Jan 15 cutover; Marissa's runbook will be attached as a gating artifact.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-exception-form.pdf (pdf, 28 KB)
